## Zero-divisor-preserving variant and its cost `[PROVED HERE]`

Hermite interpolation also gives a real-even polynomial `Q` with

`Q'(a)=-F'(a)/F(a)`                                          (10)

at every point of a finite symmetry packet.  Then

`H=e^Q F`                                                     (11)

has exactly the same zero divisor as `F`, while every selected point is critical.  Moreover

`H'/H=F'/F+Q'`,                                               (12)

so the full differential-translation fields generated by the logarithmic derivatives are equal.
Hypertranscendence versus differential algebraicity is unchanged by the zero-free DA multiplier.

The cost is growth: in general `e^Q` has order `deg Q`.  Arbitrary interpolation therefore leaves
the order-one cage.  This cost is load-bearing, not cosmetic.

## Order-one fixed-divisor rigidity `[PROVED, CLASSICAL]`

Let `F` and `G` be nonzero entire functions of order at most one with the same zeros and
multiplicities.  Hadamard factorization gives

`G(z)/F(z)=exp(az+b)`                                        (13)

for constants `a,b`.  If both functions are even, (13) at `z` and `-z` forces `a=0`.  If both are
Schwarz-real, the remaining constant is real and nonzero.  With one common normalization value,
`F=G`.

Thus the simultaneous cage

`fixed divisor + order one + FE-evenness + one normalization` (14)

has no zero-free gauge freedom.  Critical-point plasticity survives exact order through polynomial
gauges only by changing the divisor; it preserves the divisor only by paying additional growth.
This is the precise boundary at which a canonical Speiser-type statement can become meaningful.

## Exact route consequence

Speiser proved that RH is equivalent to the absence of nonreal zeros of `zeta'` in the left half of
the critical strip.  The results above prove:

1. no finite Speiser packet can be derived from an unpointed HT field, differential matroid, or
   complete algebraic power hierarchy;
2. even exact order one and scalar FE/Schwarz symmetry do not repair this finite blindness when
   polynomial divisor gauges are allowed;
3. HT plus the complete zero divisor still does not determine critical points if the order-one
   normalization is dropped;
4. only the canonical order-one fixed-divisor representative removes both gauge freedoms.

This does **not** refute Speiser's theorem or exclude a proof using its full half-strip condition for
the canonical Riemann zeta function.  It excludes implementations that expect HT structure, finite
critical-point verification, or an unpointed field/pro-field to supply the missing localization.
The surviving route must use the exact Euler-normalized representative and global critical-point
geometry; those data are not recoverable from HT alone.

theorem expGauge_affine_of_orderOne {Q F : ℂ → ℂ}

    (hFord : ∀ z, meromorphicOrderAt F z ≠ ⊤)

    (hproxF : proximity F ⊤ =o[atTop] fun r : ℝ => r ^ 2)

    simp

/-- A nonzero polynomial is bounded below outside a large disc. -/
theorem exists_radius_norm_polynomial_ge {P : Polynomial ℂ} (hP : P ≠ 0) :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ R : ℝ, ∀ z : ℂ, R ≤ ‖z‖ → c ≤ ‖P.eval z‖ := by
  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le (Nat.zero_le P.natDegree) with hdeg | hdeg
  · obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := Polynomial.natDegree_eq_zero.mp hdeg.symm
    have hune : u ≠ 0 := by
      intro h
      exact hP (by rw [← hu, h, map_zero])
    exact ⟨‖u‖, norm_pos_iff.mpr hune, 0, fun z _ => by rw [← hu]; simp⟩
  · have hdeg' : 0 < P.degree := Polynomial.natDegree_pos_iff_degree_pos.mp hdeg
    have htend : Tendsto (fun z : ℂ => ‖P.eval z‖) (Filter.cocompact ℂ) atTop :=
      Polynomial.tendsto_norm_atTop P hdeg' tendsto_norm_cocompact_atTop
    have hev : ∀ᶠ z in Filter.cocompact ℂ, (1 : ℝ) ≤ ‖P.eval z‖ :=
      htend.eventually_ge_atTop 1
    rw [← Metric.cobounded_eq_cocompact, ← comap_norm_atTop (E := ℂ),
      Filter.eventually_comap] at hev
    obtain ⟨R, hR⟩ := Filter.eventually_atTop.mp hev
    exact ⟨1, one_pos, R, fun z hz => hR ‖z‖ hz z rfl⟩

function dominates a fixed positive multiple of `ξ`, so every lower growth bound — in particular
the exact order one — is inherited. -/
theorem finitePacketGaugedXi_norm_ge {a b : Fin r → ℝ} (hb : ∀ j, 0 < b j) :

/-
# Critical-packet gauges: positivity, order, and the exponential cost

Three properties of the polynomial gauge that turns a finite packet of regular points into
critical points.

* The gauge can be taken *positive on the real axis*: interpolating an even Schwarz-real `Q` with
  `Q(a) = 1` and `Q'(a) = -F'(a)/F(a)` and setting `P = 1 + Q²` gives a real-even multiplier that is
  at least one on all of `ℝ`, hence has no real zeros, and still kills `(PF)'` on the packet
  (because `P(a) = 2` and `P'(a) = 2Q'(a)`).
* The gauge costs no growth: a polynomial factor keeps the order-one envelope
  `exp(C(1+r)log(2+r))`, only enlarging `C`.
* The zero-divisor-preserving alternative `H = e^Q F` shifts the logarithmic derivative by `Q'` and
  keeps the divisor, but it *does* cost growth: if both `F` and `e^Q F` keep subquadratic proximity,
  the fixed-divisor rigidity forces `e^Q` itself to be the exponential of an affine function.
-/

/-! ## The positive real-axis multiplier -/

theorem eval_real_of_conjEquivariant {Q : Polynomial ℂ}
    (hQconj : ∀ z, Q.eval ((starRingEnd ℂ) z) = (starRingEnd ℂ) (Q.eval z)) (x : ℝ) :
    ∃ t : ℝ, Q.eval (x : ℂ) = (t : ℂ) := by
  refine ⟨(Q.eval (x : ℂ)).re, ?_⟩
  have h := hQconj (x : ℂ)
  rw [Complex.conj_ofReal] at h
  have him : (Q.eval (x : ℂ)).im = 0 := by
    have h2 := congrArg Complex.im h
    rw [Complex.conj_im] at h2
    linarith
  exact Complex.ext rfl (by rw [him, Complex.ofReal_im])

/-- **A positive real-even critical-packet multiplier.**  On a sign- and conjugation-invariant
packet with compatible value and derivative data, the interpolating gauge can be taken of the form
`1 + Q²` with `Q` even and Schwarz-real.  The multiplier is then real and at least one on the whole
real axis — in particular it has no real zeros — while still forcing the product-rule derivative to
vanish at every packet point. -/
theorem exists_positive_real_even_polynomial_critical_packet
    {ι : Type*} [Finite ι]
    (negIdx conjIdx : ι ≃ ι)
    (w : ι → ℂ) (hw : Function.Injective w)
    (f df : ι → ℂ) (hf : ∀ i, f i ≠ 0)
    (hwneg : ∀ i, w (negIdx i) = -w i)
    (hwconj : ∀ i, w (conjIdx i) = (starRingEnd ℂ) (w i))
    (hfneg : ∀ i, f (negIdx i) = f i)
    (hdfneg : ∀ i, df (negIdx i) = -df i)
    (hfconj : ∀ i, f (conjIdx i) = (starRingEnd ℂ) (f i))
    (hdfconj : ∀ i, df (conjIdx i) = (starRingEnd ℂ) (df i)) :
    ∃ P : Polynomial ℂ,
      (∀ z, P.eval (-z) = P.eval z) ∧
      (∀ z, P.eval ((starRingEnd ℂ) z) = (starRingEnd ℂ) (P.eval z)) ∧
      (∀ x : ℝ, ∃ t : ℝ, P.eval (x : ℂ) = (t : ℂ) ∧ 1 ≤ t) ∧
      (∀ x : ℝ, P.eval (x : ℂ) ≠ 0) ∧
      ∀ i, P.eval (w i) = 2 ∧
        (derivative P).eval (w i) * f i + P.eval (w i) * df i = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨Q, hQneg, hQconj, hQ⟩ :=
    exists_real_even_polynomial_critical_packet negIdx conjIdx w hw f df hf
      hwneg hwconj hfneg hdfneg hfconj hdfconj
  have hreal := eval_real_of_conjEquivariant hQconj
  have hvalx : ∀ x : ℝ, ∃ t : ℝ, (1 + Q * Q).eval (x : ℂ) = ((1 + t ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
    intro x
    obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := hreal x
    refine ⟨t, ?_⟩
    simp only [Polynomial.eval_add, Polynomial.eval_one, Polynomial.eval_mul, ht]
    push_cast
    ring
  refine ⟨1 + Q * Q, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro z
    simp only [Polynomial.eval_add, Polynomial.eval_one, Polynomial.eval_mul, hQneg]
  · intro z
    simp only [Polynomial.eval_add, Polynomial.eval_one, Polynomial.eval_mul, hQconj, map_add,
      map_one, map_mul]
  · intro x
    obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := hvalx x
    exact ⟨1 + t ^ 2, ht, by nlinarith [sq_nonneg t]⟩
  · intro x
    obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := hvalx x
    rw [ht]
    have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < 1 + t ^ 2 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg t]
    exact Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr hpos.ne'
  · intro i
    obtain ⟨hQ1, hQ2⟩ := hQ i
    have hval : (1 + Q * Q).eval (w i) = 2 := by
      simp only [Polynomial.eval_add, Polynomial.eval_one, Polynomial.eval_mul, hQ1]
      norm_num
    refine ⟨hval, ?_⟩
    have hderiv : (derivative (1 + Q * Q)).eval (w i) = 2 * (derivative Q).eval (w i) := by
      rw [derivative_add, derivative_one, derivative_mul]
      simp only [Polynomial.eval_add, Polynomial.eval_zero, Polynomial.eval_mul, hQ1]
      ring
    rw [hval, hderiv]
    rw [hQ1] at hQ2
    linear_combination 2 * hQ2
